questions.q: What does a differential backup actually capture?
options: Every extent changed since the last full backup — not since the last differential
Every extent changed since the last differential backup only
The entire database, identical to a full backup
Only the transaction log records since the last backup of any kind
questions.explain: A differential is always relative to the last full backup, which is exactly what lets it absorb everything older than the most recent differential.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what should primarily drive how often a full backup runs?
options: The database's size and change rate — small/low-change databases can run full backups more often than large/high-change ones
A fixed industry-wide rule that all databases must use the same interval
The number of tables in the database
Whether the database uses SIMPLE or FULL recovery
questions.explain: A small, low-change database can often afford a nightly full with negligible cost, while a large, high-change OLTP database may only be able to afford one a week.

questions.q: How does log backup frequency relate to RPO (Recovery Point Objective)?
options: Log backup frequency directly sets the RPO — e.g., logs every 15 minutes means at most 15 minutes of data loss
Log backup frequency has no relationship to RPO
RPO is set only by how often full backups run
RPO can only be improved by adding more differential backups
questions.explain: Under FULL recovery, the interval between log backups is the worst-case amount of data that could be lost — that interval IS the RPO.

questions.q: Why does adding a nightly differential backup shorten the restore chain, compared to relying on full backups plus log backups alone?
options: The differential absorbs everything changed since the last full, so only log backups taken since that differential need to be applied afterward
Differential backups replace the need for a full backup entirely
Differential backups delete all prior log backups automatically
Differential backups have no effect on the restore chain
questions.explain: Without a differential, a restore might need every log backup since the last full (potentially a week's worth); with one, it only needs logs since the differential.

questions.q: A 400 GB OLTP database runs a full backup weekly and a differential nightly, but no log backups at all. The business states an RPO of 30 minutes. What does this lesson say about that setup?
options: It cannot meet a 30-minute RPO — without log backups, the worst-case data loss is however long since the last differential, far more than 30 minutes
It already meets the 30-minute RPO because differentials run nightly
RPO is unrelated to backup frequency and this setup is fine as-is
Adding more full backups, not log backups, is the only way to fix this
questions.explain: Only log backups (under FULL recovery) can deliver a tight RPO like 30 minutes — this strategy is missing log backups entirely.
